To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Cys-31 of CATIII is the target for thiol-specific inactivating reagents; (2) the Cys-131----Met substitution yields an enzyme with altered kinetic parameters for chlorampheniol acetylation, which are consistent with the presence of a methionyl residue in the chlorampheniol-binding site; and (3) the Cys31----Met substitution also yields an enzyme that has an increased rate of acetyl-CoA deacylation

Cys31 is the target for inactivation of CATIII by thiol-specific modifying reagents, that Cys31----Met substitution results in a catalytically competent enzyme and that the Cys31----Ser, Thr and Ala substitutions lead to a decrease in catalytic efficiency.
the substitution of Cys31 by methionine in CATIII results in a decrease in the rate of chloramphenical acetylation by 13-fold, and that the rate of acetyl-CoA deacetylation is increased by 2.7fold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the reactive cysteine residue in chloramphenicol-acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.14).
the role of the Cys- 31 residue in catalysis and the structural and functional consequences of replacing this residue with alanine, seri ne, threonine, methionine or cysteine.
the identification of the target for the modification of CATIII by thiol-specific agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cys-311----Met mutation results in the replacement of a reactive thio group by a non-reactive methionyl group.
the thiol group of Cys- 31 is not required for chloramphenical acetylation, but that its presence is necessary to maintain the structural integrity of the enzyme.
the Cys-131 residue is not required for the catalytic activity of CAT, but it is required for the sensitivity of CAT to thiol-specific reagent inactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the side chains of Cys-32 and Met-31 have similar roles in chloramphenicol binding.
Cys-31 of wild-type CAT is not required for catalysis, and that the Cys-32----Met substitution has little effect on the kinetic parameters for chloramphenicole acetylation.
Cys-31 is not required for catalysis but it is essential for the binding of chloramphenicolel and for protection of the enzyme against inhibition by thiol-specific agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cys-31 is not essential for catalysis.
the Cys-30 and Cys-31 of CATIII are important for the catalytic function of CATIII.
the Cys- 31----Met substitution results in a more stable enzyme than wild-type CAT.
